facts.text: My left thigh is swollen.
My left thigh hurts.

facts.item: limited movement of the left leg
facts.text: I can't move my left leg as well as normal.

facts.item: how long the thigh swelling and pain have lasted
facts.text: The swelling and pain in my left thigh and the trouble moving my leg have been going on for 3 months.
My eyesight is very poor in both eyes.
I've had type 1 diabetes since I was 14.
My sugar control has been poor for a long time; my HbA1c has been as high as 20.9%.
My diabetes has damaged the backs of my eyes (proliferative retinopathy).
My diabetes has affected my kidneys; I lose a lot of protein in my urine.
I have nerve damage from my diabetes (peripheral neuropathy).
My diabetes has also damaged the nerves that control automatic body functions (autonomic neuropathy).
I've had acute rheumatic fever.
I've had syphilis.
I keep getting urinary tract infections.
I broke my right hip (the neck of the thigh bone) and had it fixed with surgery.
I smoke 20 cigarettes a day.
I inject premixed insulin (degludec and aspart), 14 units twice a day.
Insulin is the only medicine I take.
I'm an Indigenous Australian.
I live in a remote community.

findings.name: left thigh examination
findings.result: Significant tender swelling of the left thigh without erythema, warmth or skin changes.

findings.name: sensory examination
findings.result: Stocking-distribution sensory neuropathy (assessment limited by pain).

findings.name: motor strength
findings.result: Reduced proximal left lower-limb strength (assessment limited by pain).

findings.name: funduscopic examination
findings.result: Severe proliferative diabetic retinopathy with macular oedema.

findings.name: HbA1c
findings.result: 12.4% on admission; historically as high as 20.9%.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Hemoglobin 90 g/L (normocytic anaemia); platelets 649 × 10^9/L; leukocytes 20.3 × 10^9/L; neutrophils 17.43 × 10^9/L.

findings.name: CT of the pelvis and left leg
findings.result: Ill-defined diffuse low attenuation in the left mid-thigh muscle, measuring 36 × 34 × 150 mm, without masses or collections.

findings.name: Doppler ultrasound of the left leg
MRI of the left thigh
findings.result: Marked oedema of the left anterior thigh musculature (rectus femoris, vastus medialis, vastus lateralis and adductor muscles) with muscle atrophy, fatty and fluid replacement, and subcutaneous tissue oedema; the posterior compartment is spared.

gold.reasoning: 1. Deep vein thrombosis was excluded — “A Doppler ultrasound excluded a deep vein thrombosis.” 2. Nutritional myopathy was considered but felt unlikely — “it was thought to be less likely in light of clinical presentation and imaging features.” 3. Vitamin D deficiency–related myopathy was excluded — “However, this is typically more widespread and bilateral rather than unilateral, as with our patient.” 4. Diabetic myonecrosis best fit the presentation and imaging — “The clinical presentation and progress, as well as imaging features of our case, were in keeping with diabetic myonecrosis…”
